chunks: And what Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, who said:

A man came to us in Mina and said, 'I did not catch up with the people at both stations together.' Abdullah ibn al-Mughira said to him, 'Then your Hajj is not valid.' He asked Ismail ibn 'Ammar, but he did not answer him. So Ismail entered upon Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and asked him about that. He said to him, 'If he catches up with Muzdalifah and stands at it before the sun sets on the Day of Nahr (sacrifice), then he has caught up with the Hajj.'

These two reports carry two possible meanings: one is that whoever catches up with Muzdalifah before the sun sets has caught up with the excellence and reward of Hajj, without it being meant that whoever catches it has had the obligation of the Hajj of Islam removed from him. It also carries the possibility that this ruling is specific to whoever caught up with Arafat then came to al-Mash'ar before the sun's decline, for he has caught up with the Hajj because whoever is in this state has caught up with one of the two stations at its proper time, and his Hajj is complete. And that which indicates this is what was narrated:

key_terms.الْمَوْقِفَيْنِ: The two stations, referring to Arafat and Muzdalifah
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the primary station of Hajj where the standing (wuquf) occurs
key_terms.فَرْضُ حَجَّةِ الْإِسْلاَمِ: The obligatory duty of the Hajj of Islam
key_terms.مُزْدَلِفَةَ: Muzdalifah, the station where pilgrims collect pebbles and pray after leaving Arafat
key_terms.مِنْى: Mina, a plain near Mecca where pilgrims spend the days of Tashriq
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (Eid al-Adha), the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who misses Arafat but reaches Muzdalifah before sunset on Eid al-Adha?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi presents this narration from Ibn Abi Umayr to address the juristic debate regarding whether missing one of the two primary stations (Arafat or Muzdalifah) invalidates the Hajj entirely or merely affects its perfection. The text concludes that if a pilgrim catches Muzdalifah before solar noon on the Day of Nahr, the obligation is fulfilled, reflecting the Shia view that the essential requirement is presence at one of the two key stations during its prescribed time. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Hajj jurisprudence, prioritizing the core act of standing (wuquf) over strict chronological adherence to both locations.
